findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category is unset
findings.body: The migration always does execute(... embed_category ...)[0]['id'] before checking whether a row exists. embed_category was an optional site setting, so most databases have no site_settings row (or no category whose name matches it). An empty result makes [0] nil and the migration raises NoMethodError, so upgrades that never customized embedding cannot run this migration. The same pattern on the uncategorized_category_id fallback (line 15) crashes if that row is missing.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are not normalized and are interpolated into SQL
findings.body: Existing embeddable_hosts values are inserted with raw SQL, bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation that strips http(s):// and paths. record_for_host compares URI#host (e.g. eviltrout.com) to the stored string, so previously working entries like "http://eviltrout.com" or "https://example.com/path" no longer match and embedding/referer checks fail after upgrade. The same statement interpolates the host inside single quotes, so a value containing a quote breaks the migration or injects SQL.

findings.title: Allowed-host lookup misses case and port
findings.body: record_for_host compares lower(host) to URI#host without downcasing the URI host, so a referer or embed URL whose host has any uppercase letters never matches a stored row. It also drops the port, while the host format validation allows :port and before_validation does not strip it. A saved host such as example.com:8080 can never be allowed, because the lookup host is only example.com.

findings.title: Nil host raises instead of failing validation
findings.body: before_validation calls self.host.sub! with no nil guard. create/update pass params[:embeddable_host][:host] straight through, so a missing host raises NoMethodError (500) rather than a validation error from render_json_error. record_for_host also returns false (not nil) when the URI cannot be parsed; TopicEmbed.import then calls eh.try(:category_id) on false, which raises instead of falling back to no category.

findings.title: Update and destroy 500 when the id is missing
findings.body: update and destroy load the row with where(id:).first and immediately call save_host or host.destroy. An unknown id leaves host nil, so the action raises NoMethodError instead of a 404. save_host also does not check that category_id refers to a real category, so an admin can persist a dangling category_id and later imports will create topics in a category that does not exist.

findings.title: Host regex rejects valid hosts the old setting allowed
findings.body: validates_format_of requires a dotted hostname whose final label is 2–5 letters. That rejects IP addresses, localhost, and real TLDs longer than 5 characters (for example .museum or .cloud). Those values could be stored in the old embeddable_hosts setting and are inserted by the migration without validation, but they cannot be saved or edited through the new admin API.

findings.title: Plural id hydration assumes a non-null array
findings.body: The new *_ids branch always calls obj[k].map. Any rest-serialized payload that includes a plural foreign key as null (rather than []) now throws while hydrating, which breaks find/findAll for that type. Previously only singular *_id keys were handled, and only when a match was found.
